Q2497112.label: Luxembourgian European Constitution referendum, 2005
Q2497112.summary: A referendum on ratifying the proposed European Constitution was held in Luxembourg on 10 July 2005. The referendum was Luxembourg's first since 1937. On 28 June 2005 Parliament approved the constitution in advance of the referendum, and although the referendum was consultative, parliament agreed to abide by the results.

Q1073752.label: Hungarian Working People's Party
Q1073752.summary: The Hungarian Working People's Party was the ruling Marxist-Leninist party of Hungary from 1948 to 1956.

Q2627160.label: 2004 Serbian presidential election
Q2627160.summary: Presidential elections were held in the Republic of Serbia on Sunday, 13 June 2004. As no candidate received a majority of the vote, a second round was held on Sunday, 27 June. Boris Tadić, the pro-western Democratic Party's candidate, was the eventual victor with 54% of the vote.

Q1204824.label: 2007 Greek legislative election
Q1204824.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Greece on Sunday, 16 September 2007 to elect the 300 members of the Hellenic Parliament. The leading party for a second term was New Democracy under the leadership of Kostas Karamanlis with 42%, followed by George Papandreou and PASOK with 38%.

Q944216.label: Vilis Krištopans
Q944216.img: Member of the European Parliament for Latvia Vilis Krištopans.jpg
Q944216.summary: Vilis Krištopans is a Latvian politician who served as the prime minister of Latvia from 26 November 1998 to 15 July 1999.

Q19362904.label: assassination of Boris Nemtsov
Q19362904.desc: 2015 murder of a Russian opposition politician
Q19362904.img: There are flowers and candles near the site of the murder of Boris Nemtsov cropped.jpg
Q19362904.summary: On 27 February 2015, Boris Nemtsov, a Russian politician opposed to the government of Vladimir Putin, was assassinated as he crossed the Bolshoy Moskvoretsky Bridge in central Moscow at 23:31 local time. An unknown assailant fired seven or eight shots from a Makarov pistol.

Q85224024.label: Bombing of Ferrara in World War II
Q85224024.wiki: Bombing of Ferrara in World War II
Q85224024.summary: The bombing of Ferrara was a series of attacks by the United States Army Air Force and the Royal Air Force on the Italian city of Ferrara, Emilia-Romagna, during the final two years of World War II. The purpose of these raids was to disable the city's marshalling yard, but they also resulted in considerable collateral damage to the city itself, and over a thousand deaths among the population.

Q4870744.label: Battle of Chuncheon
Q4870744.summary: The Battle of Chuncheon was one of a series of coordinated attacks beginning on 25 June 1950 that marked the beginning of the Korean War.

Q118162520.label: Battle of Nyala
Q118162520.summary: The Battle of Nyala was a battle for control of Nyala, the capital of South Darfur in Sudan, between the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), and the Sudanese Armed Forces during the ongoing Darfur campaign. The first battle occurred between 15 and 20 April 2023, during which hundreds were reported dead. A civilian-brokered ceasefire paused the fighting by April 20. Sporadic clashes broke out between May and July. In August 2023, the RSF launched an offensive on the city. The SAF launched air campaigns against the RSF in Nyala, with many civilian casualties in Taiba and El Matar.

Q170072.label: Dutch Republic
aliases: Republic of the Seven United Netherlands
Republic of the Seven United Provinces
Q170072.summary: The Republic of the Seven United Netherlands, also known as the United Provinces, and referred to in historiography as the Dutch Republic, was a confederation and great power that existed from 1588 until the Batavian Revolution in 1795. It was a predecessor state of the present-day Netherlands and the first independent Dutch nation state.

Q5720.label: Valencian Community
Q5720.summary: The Valencian Community is an autonomous community of Spain. It is the fourth most populous Spanish autonomous community after Andalusia, Catalonia and the Community of Madrid with more than 5 million inhabitants. Its eponymous capital and most populous city is Valencia, the third-largest city and metropolitan area in Spain. It is located along the Mediterranean coast on the east side of the Iberian Peninsula. It borders Catalonia to the north, Aragon and Castilla–La Mancha to the west, and Murcia to the south, and the Balearic Islands are to its east.

Q212056.label: Mongolian People's Republic
Q212056.summary: The Mongolian People's Republic (MPR) was the Mongolian communist state that existed from 1924 to 1992 that self-designated first as a people's democratic state and later as a socialist state. The Mongolian People's Revolutionary Party was enshrined as the leading force of state and society; it occupied the historical region of Outer Mongolia. Geographically positioned between the Soviet Union and China, the MPR became the world's second communist state. It was the first Soviet satellite state, and remained so for its entire existence, longer than any other Soviet satellite.

Q137816.label: Taiwan under Japanese rule
Q137816.summary: The island of Taiwan, along with the Penghu Islands, became an annexed territory of the Empire of Japan in 1895, when the Qing dynasty ceded Fujian-Taiwan Province in the Treaty of Shimonoseki after the Japanese victory in the First Sino-Japanese War. After Japanese forces crushed the consequent Republic of Formosa resistance movement, Japan ruled Taiwan for 50 years. Its capital was located in Taihoku (Taipei), the seat of the Governor-General of Taiwan.
